Definition: a quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of G4225; how much (as an indefinite), i.e. in size or (figuratively) dignity:--how great (large).
BiblicalUsage: Pelikos asks how great, how large. Paul tells the Galatians to see how large a letter he has written with his own hand, and Hebrews says to consider how great Melchizedek was, to whom even Abraham gave a tenth of the spoils.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hold is that greatness is measured by what God honours: Abraham gave a tenth to Melchizedek because he knew a greater priest when he saw one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
